narre.kind: review-attention rating model, task-adapted to sentence scoring
narre.paper: Chen, Zhang, Liu, Ma. Neural Attentional Rating Regression with Review-level Explanations. WWW 2018.
narre.mechanism: Real trained CNN+two-sided-attention network (baselines/published/neural/narre.py, ported from the official TF1 model.py), trained on rating regression over a temporal-safe, 5-core-filtered review corpus per dataset (scripts/train_published_neural.py). PEER scores each candidate review with NARRE's item-side attention weight, whose context is that review's author -- the paper's own review-usefulness signal, applied directly to PEER's candidate pool instead of the paper's own held-out review set.
narre.adaptation_notes: Single shared word-embedding table for user/item text (paper uses two independently-sized tables for the same underlying vocabulary). Rating-prediction head (NCF interaction + biases) is trained but unused at PEER inference time -- only the attention sub-network is queried.

hrdr.kind: rating-pattern-guided review-attention model, task-adapted to sentence scoring
hrdr.paper: Liu, Wang, Peng, Wu, Gan, Pan, Jiao. Hybrid neural recommendation with joint deep representation learning of ratings and reviews. Neurocomputing 374 (2020): 77-85.
hrdr.mechanism: Real trained CNN+attention network (baselines/published/neural/hrdr.py, ported from the official PyTorch source), attention context = an MLP over the (frozen) user-item rating matrix row/column, trained on rating regression over the same temporal-safe, 5-core corpus as NARRE. PEER scores each candidate review with the item tower's attention weight (context = the target item's rating-matrix column).
hrdr.adaptation_notes: The released repo excerpt we could inspect does not include the prediction head (models/prediction.py); we implemented a standard NCF-style head (dot-product + user/item/global bias) in the same spirit as NARRE's, documented as our own completion of that missing piece -- unused at PEER inference time, same as NARRE.

a2spr.kind: aspect-sentiment vector similarity (not a neural model)
a2spr.paper: Huang et al. 2020. Personalized Review Recommendation based on Users' Aspect Sentiment.
a2spr.mechanism: Cosine similarity between the candidate sentence's per-aspect sentiment vector and the target user's aspect-sentiment profile built from their review history (peer/aspect_sentiment.py). Aspect assignment reuses PEER's own upstream aspect extraction/canonicalization instead of the paper's TF-IDF step.

erra_r.kind: personalized dense retrieval + aspect-salience boost, task-adapted to sentence scoring
erra_r.paper: Explainable Recommendation with Personalized Review Retrieval and Aspect Learning. ACL 2023 (arXiv:2306.12657).
erra_r.mechanism: Dense retrieval: cosine similarity between each candidate sentence's embedding and a (user-history + metadata) query embedding, boosted for candidates covering the (user,item) pair's top-n most salient shared aspects.
erra_r.adaptation_notes: The paper's explanation-generation stage (final step after retrieval) does not apply to PEER's selection task and is not reproduced.

prag.kind: small trained personalized retriever, task-adapted to sentence scoring
prag.paper: Xie, Singh, McAuley, Majumder. Factual and Informative Review Generation for Explainable Recommendation. EMNLP 2023 (arXiv:2209.12613).
prag.mechanism: A small MLP (scripts/train_prag_retriever.py) trained to estimate the target review's embedding from (user-history, metadata) embeddings; candidates are ranked by cosine similarity to that estimate -- the paper's retriever mechanism at a scale that fits this project.
prag.adaptation_notes: The paper's retriever uses transformer blocks over a much larger training corpus; architecture details beyond the abstract were not available to us, so this is a deliberately scaled-down stand-in for the same mechanism, not a claim of matching the paper's retriever exactly. The generator stage is not applicable to PEER's selection task.
